\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرمایه} (sarmâye)}{سرمایه (sarmâye)}]{\fa{سرمایه} (sarmâye) — capital, an investment}

\label{lesson:FA-C412-sarmaye}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for in debt, then the Persian for a creditor.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرمایه}}
\textbf{\fa{سرمایه}} (\emph{sarmâye}) — \textquotedblleft{}capital, an investment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{با} \fa{سرمایه} \fa{کمی} \fa{یک} \fa{فروشگاه} \fa{باز} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u bâ sarmâye-ye kami yek forushgâh bâz kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He opened a shop with a little capital.
\end{quote}

\emph{Sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} + \emph{mâye} \textquotedblleft{}substance, stock\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{سرمایه}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{sar} \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{} + \emph{mâye} \textquotedblleft{}substance, stock\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian \textquotedblleft{}essence, substance\textquotedblright{}. Capital is the head stock of a business.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarmâye}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarmâye}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sarmâye}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for in debt, then the Persian for a creditor, then say \emph{sarmâye} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{سرمایه} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Capital, an investment\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرمایه} \fa{گذاری} \fa{کردن} (sarmâye gozâri …)}{سرمایه گذاری کردن (sarmâye gozâri …)}]{\fa{سرمایه} \fa{گذاری} \fa{کردن} (sarmâye gozâri kardan) — to invest}

\label{lesson:FA-C412-sarmaye-gozari-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a creditor, then the Persian for capital.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرمایه} \fa{گذاری} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{سرمایه} \fa{گذاری} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{sarmâye gozâri kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to invest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{شرکت} \fa{کوچک} \fa{سرمایه} \fa{گذاری} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedaram dar yek sherkat-e kuchek sarmâye gozâri kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father invested in a small company.
\end{quote}

\emph{Sarmâye} + \emph{gozâri} \textquotedblleft{}placing\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{gozâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{kardan}. Takes \emph{dar}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{سرمایه} \fa{گذاری} \fa{کردن}} is native Persian, built from \emph{sarmâye} \textquotedblleft{}capital\textquotedblright{} + \emph{gozâri} \textquotedblleft{}placing\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{gozâr-}, the present stem of \emph{gozâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to put\textquotedblright{}, + \emph{kardan}. To invest is to place capital.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarmâye gozâri kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sarmâye gozâri kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sarmâye gozâri kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a creditor, then the Persian for capital, then say \emph{sarmâye gozâri kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{سرمایه} \fa{گذاری} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To invest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سهام} (sahâm)}{سهام (sahâm)}]{\fa{سهام} (sahâm) — shares, stock}

\label{lesson:FA-C412-saham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for capital, then the Persian for to invest.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سهام}}
\textbf{\fa{سهام}} (\emph{sahâm}) — \textquotedblleft{}shares, stock\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{سهام} \fa{یک} \fa{شرکت} \fa{بزرگ} \fa{را} \fa{خرید}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u sahâm-e yek sherkat-e bozorg râ kharid.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She bought shares in a big company.
\end{quote}

The Arabic broken plural of \emph{sahm} \textquotedblleft{}a share, a portion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{سهام}} is an Arabic broken plural of \emph{sahm} \textquotedblleft{}part, portion\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB lists as the source of Persian \emph{sahm}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بورس} (burs)}{بورس (burs)}]{\fa{بورس} (burs) — the stock exchange}

\label{lesson:FA-C412-burs}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to invest, then the Persian for shares.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بورس}}
\textbf{\fa{بورس}} (\emph{burs}) — \textquotedblleft{}the stock exchange\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{قیمت} \fa{سهام} \fa{در} \fa{بورس} \fa{پایین} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{qeymat-e sahâm dar burs pâyin âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Share prices fell on the stock exchange.
\end{quote}

A French loan. It also turns up in \emph{bursiye} \textquotedblleft{}scholarship\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{بورس}} is usually traced to French \emph{bourse} \textquotedblleft{}stock exchange; purse\textquotedblright{}, from Late Latin \emph{bursa} \textquotedblleft{}purse\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{ورشکسته} (varshekaste)}{ورشکسته (varshekaste)}]{\fa{ورشکسته} (varshekaste) — bankrupt}

\label{lesson:FA-C412-varshekaste}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for shares, then the Persian for the stock exchange.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{ورشکسته}}
\textbf{\fa{ورشکسته}} (\emph{varshekaste}) — \textquotedblleft{}bankrupt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آن} \fa{شرکت} \fa{سال} \fa{گذشته} \fa{ورشکسته} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ân sherkat sâl-e gozashte varshekaste shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That company went bankrupt last year.
\end{quote}

\emph{Var} + \emph{shekaste} \textquotedblleft{}broken\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Varshekast shodan} — to go bankrupt.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{ورشکسته}} is native Persian, built on \emph{shekaste} \textquotedblleft{}broken\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{shekastan} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to PIE \emph{skeyd-} \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}. A bankrupt business is broken.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
